title: engine-config v1
description: Which harness, provider and model each part of the Horde runs on, and later other settings, as one layer of rules (engines plan step E3; engine-settings design, sections 2 to 4). One schema for every layer that is a file: L0 built-in, L1 the user's, L4 live. L2, a project's own file, is not built until a repo needs one, and the checker refuses it. Providers, aliases and profiles are defined only in L0 and L1; revision belongs to L4 alone; a tuner's rule and an expiry only to L4. Never holds a secret: a credential is the NAME of an environment variable, or the harness's own login. Rules a draft-07 schema cannot say are core/EngineConfig.ps1's (Test-HordeEngineConfig), listed in its header.

revision.description: L4 only: compared and swapped by every writer of the live rules (engines E7).

model.description: An alias name, or a concrete model id.

credential.description: harness-login: the harness's own login, which is the user's subscription, so Horde passes nothing; legal only on a harness whose descriptor names this provider as its nativeProvider (the subscription rule). env: the NAME of an environment variable holding the key, read at launch and never stored (agent-engines decision 9). The design's os-store kind is not built.

protocol.description: The wire format the endpoint speaks, named as schema/agent-descriptor.v1 names them. A harness may use the provider only if its descriptor lists this protocol (the wire-format rule).

endpoint.description: Absent: the harness's own default endpoint for the protocol.

models.description: An allowlist of concrete ids. When present, a model outside it is a finding.

lacks.description: Capabilities of core/capabilities.json this provider removes from any harness that uses it.

model.description: Absent: the harness's own default model, so no model flag is passed.

match.description: Every key must match (AND); an empty match matches every target. Ranks for specificity are engines E4's.

set.description: Settings by key. The keys, their values and the layers each may be set in are core/config-keys.json's, checked by core/EngineConfig.ps1, so a new setting (metrics.level, admission.tier, remote.*) is one registry entry rather than a schema change. profile expands to its harness, provider and model at the rule's layer and specificity.

writtenBy.description: Set by the program that writes the rule: user by hand, cli by horde config set, tuner by the admission tuner, which writes only live rules (engine-settings decision 9).

until.description: L4 only: when the rule stops applying.
